utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You won't know what you are explaining because you don't know my problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My problem is that this document on the screen is giving the number 5 for the month of August. The chart is dealing with wounded people for the period August to December.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's dealing with wounded people, as I understood the chart, who were wounded by snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For a period August to December.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, for the period of August -- yes, August to December on a monthly basis, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On a monthly basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure, in August if we look at the very first--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go to that chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- part. In the month of August, as I understand this chart, five individuals were injured by sniper fire. In the month of September, five individuals were injured by sniper fire. In the month of October, 16 individuals were injured by sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies, I'm with you. I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, let's make sure I'm actually interpreting the chart correctly because if I am making a mistake I shouldn't be doing this examination in this particular way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Am I correct in what I just said in my conversation with His Honour that what we have here is a monthly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Breakdown.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- breakdown - thank you - of the number of people who were injured by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Do you mean this -- the B/C/S version that I see, the individual reports from the operations theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again can we have page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the end of this, you can see the source where the protocols kept at the emergency centre of the State Hospital in Sarajevo which means that this is the breakdown of all victims who were brought to and treated at the centre. Some of these victims were operated in the operations theatres, some, because they were severely injured, were not even admitted to hospital, nor taken to the surgery because they were treated at outpatient clinics and they were sent home. So these reports that you see here in this chart were based on the protocols that we kept on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. I'm ... [Previous translation continues] ... the significance of this particular chart. As I understand the chart for the month of August, five people were injured by sniper fire and treated at the emergency centre: September 5, October 16, November 12, December 5 for a total of 43 individuals; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The further breakdown is to whether or not they were adults, children or armed forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of whether or not they were armed forces, can you tell from looking at this chart whether or not the individuals who are designated as being wounded by sniper fire who are in the armed forces were wounded by sniper fire while they were engaged in military operations, by looking at this chart?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: No, by looking at this chart, no, nor did we keep such record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to now going back, I want to go to the month -- we've determined that for the month of August that five were injured and we found out that looking at the monthly information that it compares, it's a one-to-one correlation. For the month of September --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go to the month of September, which I believe is page 13 in the English and page 33 in the B/C/S. Once again if we could go down to, I believe it's item number 10 or once again the number of newly injured by sniper is five?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, my screen I have for the English, I have the report for the August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You are right. Try page 37. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And on the B/C/S screen I seem to have a list of doctors, or what is that DR standing for, for the names of the people in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, these doctors were sniped too, all of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, obviously we are running into a couple of different problems with this document. I notice -- I note what the Judge says about this document which is there are a number of doctors on it. If you look at -- which is one issue. If you look at item number 10, under item number 10, does it indicate under item number 10 the number newly injured by snipers was five; is that what says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does he see it in the B/C/S. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking the question under item number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't see item number 10 on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure you do, look on the right-hand side of the screen, it says 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here under item 10 in the B/C/S version it says newly injured by sniper 5, and the same thing is repeated in English, number of newly injured by sniper 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you go to the next month, which is the month of October --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that can I be clear on why we don't have this list of doctors on the English and what does this -- are these the same documents, are these two versions of the same document or are we dealing with two different documents here? There's a whole list of doctors on the one document and we don't see it on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think, I understand what you are saying. I think what we have is we have something that's been cleaned up in the English version. Let me ask the following question:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated you do read English. Could you look at the English version of this document and go to -- down to item number 5 on the English version, and under that it says list of names and numbers, and then under item number 6 it says list of names and numbers. Do you see that and can you recognise that in English?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. Under 5 is the number of surgeons -- number of surgeries per surgeon so those surgeons who were team leaders. And it also indicates the total number of surgeries performed by Dr. Nakas for instance, 103; Dr. Vuletic, 12; Dr. Dzogovic [phoen], 9; and so on and so forth. Under 6 we have the list of surgeons as first assistants in the operation theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this analysis or not. But what has happened here, is if you look at the total number of surgeries that were done under item number 1 which is the same in both documents, that being 209, that the difference between these two documents is there is a breakdown here by doctor who performed the medical procedure and in the English what you have is a breakdown not by the doctor that performed the medical procedure, but rather by subject matter?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Here in the English version, the portion that is missing is the information per doctor. It just states that there is a list of names following and the number of surgeries or medical procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. That creates other issues, but those aren't issues for you, those are issues for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I guess the witness is correct and items 1 to 4 are globular summaries. In fact, they say exactly the same. It's number 5 which is itemised, and number 6 which is itemised in the one version and not itemised in the other version; and I think to that extent I'm now with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I thank you for that intervention, because I've been trying to figure out a variety of things with these documents. Could we go to the next month which would be October. And in October, so we don't have to jump back and forth between all the pages, if you take it from me, and Mr. Cannata can double-check, the total number of individuals who were injured and treated in the emergency centre were 16. If we could go to page 35 of the English and 35 of the B/C/S. Or is it 34? Okay. Now, if we could go to item number 10 once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As I read item number 10, it says "number of newly injured by sniper, 7." And that seems to be the number both in the English and from what I can tell, and help me here, if I'm looking at number 10 in the B/C/S, that would be the middle entry where it says 7?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes. What we have here is the number of surgeries and the type of wounding. Where it relates to snipers the number is 7, so this is the number of surgeries performed in operation theatres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to the information that's contained on the page of the chart where it indicates the number of 16, could you tell us what the difference is for the months of August and September where there was a one-to-one correlation with a number of 5 between the English, B/C/S and the chart, and October where you have an indication of the number 7, and the chart indicates that there was a wounding of an additional 9 people?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: The difference is in the severity of the injures. In August and September of 1994, these were all seriously wounded, so they requested surgery in the operation theatre under general anaesthesia. In October, we had seven such operations of people wounded by snipers, and altogether, the emergency room took care of 16 patients which means that this remaining number of 9 could be treated in the examination room. So they did not request any general anaesthesia. Possibly the wounds just needed to be stitched up or cleaned or something similar. So these were injured that did not call for an operation to be performed in the operation theatre. So this is the number which you can see here of the real surgeries carried out under general anaesthesia, so this is the difference that you can see: The number of operations, the surgeries, and the number of patients treated altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand your answer but I'm somewhat confused. Looking at the document in front of us it says for item number 10 it doesn't indicate anything with regard to the issue of surgeries it says number newly injured by sniper 7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith look at number 10 and read the line directly opposite number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Number of surgeries per type of wound. Okay, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that list is dealing with surgeries. And the surgeries that were dealt with that resulted from sniping were 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, my question is, where do I find the additional nine -- where do I find in this document here the additional nine snipers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But does this document purport to deal with the globular figure of snipers or does it purport to deal with the surgeries?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My understanding was that this document here is a compilation of the breakout by month which we were discussing in terms of each of these documents, but let's find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that was your interpretation which you put to the witness with respect to the month of August. But I don't know -- before that I haven't had the witness give us that testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's find out. That's the best way of doing it. Let's find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the documents, the 35 pages of documents that are attached to the chart, did you go through an analysis of those 35 documents to make a determination of whether or not the chart as it's constituted, that being citizens of Sarajevo wounded by the snips and treated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but before we confuse the witness, I would just like to have it clear on the record that page 35, the document that is now on e-court, is a report for the surgeries carried out. The chart at page 3, which the doctor has been asked to compare with the report deals with surgeries and other medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought the doctor actually did explain that a couple of minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, it is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that here he is dealing with surgeries, which is why I intervened when Mr. Guy-Smith persisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So I don't know whether sitting where he is without all these documents in front of him he will be able to tell you where you will find the remaining nine if he doesn't have the documents, but you go ahead and let's see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All I can do is work with the documents that were given to me by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All I'm saying is let the witness have the documents that you are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it's probably easier to do this in hard copy than it is electronically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Technology has its own limitations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I were to do it, I would do it in hard copy rather than electronically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do it the way you want to do it, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might supply the witness with a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Mr. Usher, can you help us and can the opposite counsel please have a look at that document before it goes to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I only have the hard copy in English. And I don't know if that will constitute a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, if give you the hard copy only in English will that constitute a problem for you in being able to read it, or are you okay reading it in English?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: That should be enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all you'll note there's some highlighting on the document, the highlighting has no significance whatsoever it was my attempt to understand what was going in the document. So you don't need to pay any attention to that at all. Looking at the document and starting with month since we'll go back now of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document are we looking at, the one on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the hard copy for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I want to know is the hard copy the same thing on the screen or is it something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm about to go through that with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you can go to page 4 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can't put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Since the witness is provided only with the English copy, can I suggest that we make reference to the B/C/S either on the ELMO or e-court, but it's been solved, thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What about the B/C/S, Mr. Cannata?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We have a B/C/S copy now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why don't we do this because it might be of some assistance, on the screen let us put up on the screen page, I believe it's, 1 of the English and the chart, just the chart, in 3 of the B/C/S. So that will just be a fixed document which is the first page of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can't see e-court and ELMO at the same time on the screen ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's one of the reasons I hate this electronic system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can either give us all copies of these documents in hard copy, sir, we are welcome to have them in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All right. Well, I did not expect to be engaged in a hard copy discussion and don't have hard copy distribution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. Then let's go the best way we can bearing in mind that on our screens [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We cannot simultaneously look at the ELMO and e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine we will dedicate it to this page and go back. I have figured out a way of doing it. If we could go to page 4 of the hard copy document in English, which is where we started our journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at this document, and if we could have this now up on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Going to item number 10, when it deals with number of surgeries per type of wound, it says: "Number of newly injured by sniper, 5." Correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we look at the top of this particular document in terms of what it identifies, it identifies a report on number and type of surgeries for August 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we were to go back to the chart, is the entry of the number 5 that is reflected on the chart --

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- the same as the entry in number 10 which is reflected on page 4 under the designation of number of newly injured by sniper?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the identical number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to October, 1994, the chart indicates an entry of 16 individuals injured by sniper; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: First of all, did you have an opportunity to review these documents to see whether there was a correlation between the entry on the chart of that number and the breakout sheet for that particular month, that being the month of October 1994?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: The numbers can be corresponding if these were such injures that called for a surgery under general anaesthesia. If these were minor injures that only called for treatment in the check-up room, then the numbers should not necessarily correspond because one of these reports has to do with severe injures which called for general anaesthesia surgeries. So this can simply mean that there were more minor injures in October so that only seven of them called for general anaesthesia surgeries. Whereas nine of them were treated in the check-up room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at the chart for November of 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, can you please start your question from scratch because you overlapped with the interpretation --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- and you were not transcribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With your previous answer in mind, can we look at the entry in the chart for November of 1994, which indicates the total number of wounded and treated in the emergency centre for snipers was 12; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 33 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you like, I think we can also have that up for you in B/C/S in hard copy, if you would like that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: This is sufficient, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What item are we looking at now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Trying to get to any -- page 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we go down once again to 10, it says number of newly injured by sniper is 5; correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the report, the monthly report that was done for November 1994 what information contained in the monthly report for November of 1994 reflects the additional 7 individuals who are claimed having been wounded by sniper fire in the chart that's been produced? How do we find that information, sir?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: You can find it in the protocols of the emergency centre where these patients were received, checked up, some of them because of the severity of the wounds were operated on, and this is the number of 5, the rest of them were treated on the spot, and they went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could take a look at page 32 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is as I understand it a report of the emergency centre for the month of November 1994. Is this the protocol that you were referring to when you discuss the issue of the protocol of the emergency centre?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular document, could you tell us where we would find the corresponding figure of 12 individuals injured by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: You can find them among this total number of 43. This is the total number. So they are a part of this number and then also you have the segmentation into members of armed forces or civilians, so next line is the number of admitted patients, those admitted to the hospital. There was a total of 21. Out of these 21 admitted patients, 10 were members of armed forces, and 11 were civilians. These were small surgical interventions so those that were not carried out in operation theatres; so this is this number 14 and among them you will find the remaining 7 out of that number that we had in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So from -- I'm supposed to determine, if I understand it, from the number 14 that you've just discussed with us, that we pull out that 7 individuals to make up the 12 that are on the chart?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How do you -- how do you do that? What indicates to you on this document here that we are looking at right now, which is the report of the emergency centre for the month of November, that any individuals who were treated were treated for sniper fire? There's no indication here at all, is there?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: No, not on this part. This is something that's registered in the protocol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this is something that I think the doctor has been trying to explain, Mr. Guy-Smith. This document is not drafted to give you that information. It doesn't purport to give that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you would take a quick look at the documents that were supplied by the Prosecution in support of the chart that's in front of you, could you tell me whether there are other documents that exist that would be of assistance for us to understand the numbers that are contained in the chart, or whether these are all the documents that exist?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, I'm afraid that my learned friend misstates the evidence. This chart was not produced on the basis of documents that the doctor was provided with by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am sorry, I didn't mean to leave that impression. And if I did, they were supplied to the Defence in support of this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. You see the thing is, I don't even know whether Mr. Cannata referred the witness to this document in chief. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He referred the witness to the chart. He then moved into admission a 37-page document which included, as its front page, the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The documents that we have been examining are the monthly breakouts as we understand it with regard to the chart that was shown to the witness; and the document, as I was supplied it by the Prosecution, the chart is page 1 of 37 and the various entries that we have been discussing as part of that 37-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And Your Honours, for ease of reference, I will direct your attention to page 57, line 19 to 58 to line 5 of today's transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Thank you. Now, I don't dispute if these are documents that are in evidence, that's fine, but the only thing is just by looking at the headings and the way that they are drafted, I'm left with the impression that these documents are drafted for different purposes; and the purpose for which you were asking the witness didn't seem to be apparent from this document. You asked the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are we referring now to the report of the emergency centre for the month of November?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm trying to look at ... I'm trying to look for the question that you put to the witness which has now disappeared. I can't see it. Okay. I'm not going to waste more time on it. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this about this set of documents then, see if we can get clarification. Are the 35 pages that follow the chart documents that can be used to support the conclusions that are found in the chart? That's my first question.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: In part.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are there other documents above and beyond those 35 pages of documents?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, there are protocols, ledgers with protocols.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you refer to protocol, are you referring to a protocol different than the protocol that is presently up on the ELMO? I'm sorry, different than protocol that we were referring to before which was a report of the emergency centre for the month of -- for any particular month? Are you referring to a different protocol?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: I'm referring to the ledger consisting of protocols, in this protocol every patient is recorded individually by name. These wer monthly reports that were used by me as a manager when I needed to organise our work and present our work to somebody else, and this is why in this document we had the number of newly injured, injured children, dead on arrival, and so on; reports from the gynaecology on the number of newly born children. So this is a report that was used by me to report to the Federal Ministry of Health, to the WHO, and whoever requested data from us. In these kind of protocols, or in these kinds of reports, we never had segmented data on the number of injured by snipers, numbers of injured by shell fire, and so on. We simply had reports on the admissions, surgeries, civilians or military, and so on. So on these reports, we did not register shell fire versus sniper fire. And the tables were compiled following the request of the Prosecution to provide the number of people who were treated because they were injured by sniper fire. This is why these numbers that were provided in the charts are included into this general number, but in this report, they are not segmented as such. The official source of report are protocols which are our official documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have page 35 of 37 up on the screen. And I do -- the markings on it are my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular document, you said, so I understand: "We simply had reports on admissions, surgeries, civilians or military and so on, so on these reports we did not register shell fire versus sniper file and the tables were provided following the request of the Prosecution." And you go on. Now, with regard to this particular document, if you would scroll down, please, is the information that is contained in part number 10 concerning the number of surgeries per type of wound, is that information that was compiled at the time, and by that I mean at the time -- at the conclusion of the month, or is this document a document that was compiled at the request of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: This is a document that was compiled at the end of the month. This is a copy of a document that I received at the end of each month. So it was not compiled upon the request of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... identifies the very kind of injures, the very kind of injure that is you just indicated you did not identify and by that I mean shrapnel sniper, does it not?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: This document from the surgical ward does say that, but the documents coming from the emergency ward do not say that. So when we are talking about surgeries carried out under total anaesthesia, then you have this breakdown per type of wounds which caused the surgery, because in most cases the amount of material that had to be used and the very length of surgical intervention depended on the type of wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I note the time and I would say this is an appropriate time to break. I have probably quite a few more questions for the gentleman, and I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In any case we wouldn't be able to excuse him because there are still re-examination. Sorry, sir, unfortunately we've run out of time, we've got to give the court to another case to sit. We'll have to postpone to tomorrow. In Courtroom I, not this one, Courtroom I at 9.00 in the morning. If you could be there at 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned to tomorrow morning 9.00. Courtroom I.
